title: Bacterial Plating and Dilution
author: Lachlan Munro
materials: Continues until 10 serial dilutions have been performed.

steps.title: Prepare agar plates
steps.instruction: Fill each Nunc Omnitray with 30 mL of melted agar, place the trays on a flat surface and allow the agar to dry so that the surface is level across the plate.

steps.title: Preload plates with samples and buffer
steps.instruction: Add the bacterial sample to column 1 of each tray; add 90 µL of dilution buffer or media to columns 2‑12 of the same tray.

steps.title: Calibrate pipette tip height
steps.instruction: Adjust the pipette so that the tip just barely touches the agar surface (the “top of the well”) when positioned over a well.

steps.title: Spot initial sample onto agar
steps.instruction: Using a clean tip, dispense 5 µL of the bacterial sample from column 1 onto the agar surface of the corresponding well.

steps.title: Perform ten‑fold serial dilutions and spot each dilution
steps.instruction: Repeat the following for dilution numbers 1 through 10:

substeps.instruction: Transfer 10 µL from the current column into the next column containing 90 µL of dilution buffer, then mix thoroughly.
Spot 5 µL of the newly diluted sample onto the agar surface of the corresponding well.

steps.title: Replace tips and process next plate
steps.instruction: Discard the used tip, pick up a new clean tip, and repeat steps 1‑5 for the next agar plate (up to 5 plates, 8 wells per plate, total ≤ 40 samples).
